instrument: A VPC built for this case alone: 10.61.0.0/16, a public subnet holding a NAT gateway and a private subnet holding the runtime's ENIs, each subnet on its own explicitly associated route table. Three VPC-mode AgentCore Runtimes created in sequence from the same public image (public.ecr.aws/nginx/nginx:stable) and the same execution role, differing only in whether the private route table carried 0.0.0.0/0 -> the NAT gateway. Every arm measured on BOTH channels: the create-time terminal status with its failureReason, and an actual InvokeAgentRuntime.
limitations: one Region, one AZ, one image, one arm per condition — planned_n is None for this case, so n=1 is the pre-registered denominator and not a shortfall
the private subnet had no VPC endpoints at all, so this measures the absence of ANY egress path and not the absence of a NAT gateway specifically
single calendar day: under PREREGISTRATION.yaml's reproduction_before_amendment rule a day-2 replication is required before the document is amended on this result

rederived.audit_trail: the first scoring is archived unchanged at evidence/.../F5-7b/analysis.json; this write used store=None so it could not touch it
rederived.changed: the READING of the archived arms, not the observation
instrument_fix: PULL_MARKERS no longer contains 'timeout' or 'timed out' — words a client-side socket error matches and a service-supplied failureReason does not need
pull_evidence() now returns `ambiguous` BY CONSTRUCTION when an invoke carries no HTTP status and no request id, before either marker list is consulted
the branch table moved out of main() into decide(), so this re-scoring ran the producer's own code rather than a transcription of it
rederived.still_owed: a run with a working invoke channel, or the runtime's CloudWatch log stream, before this case has been measured at all. See results/FINDING-F5-7B.md section 4.
rederived.what_was_not_re-measured: everything. No AWS resource was created, no arm was re-run, and the arms, signatures, network report and residue in this file are the archived ones byte for byte. Only pull_evidence, verdict_reading and the record were recomputed.
rederived.why: The first scoring labelled all three arms `pull_failed` on the strength of a client-side botocore socket timeout, because PULL_MARKERS contained 'timeout'/'timed out' and bucket_failure() was written to read a SERVICE-supplied failureReason. The three invokes returned 70082 / 70077 / 70073 ms — a 9 ms spread over three independent calls, which is a constant read as a measurement. An invoke that received no HTTP status and no request id cannot name the fetch or any other step, and with this image (nginx serves :80, AgentCore's contract is :8080) a SUCCESSFUL pull produces the same silence as a failed one. So the arms are `ambiguous`, and the verdict is reached through the instrument branch rather than the pair table.
rederived.why_the_published_verdict_was_neverthele: The mislabelling could only ever emit `pull_failed`. The oracle's TRUE requires the pair (pull_failed, pull_succeeded) and its FALSE requires pull_succeeded on the no-route arm, so the defect could not manufacture either verdict — it could only push toward INCONCLUSIVE, which is where the case already sat. Nothing wrong was published. What was wrong was the recorded REASON, and the repair it invited: 'the arms produced a pair the oracle does not name' points a future reader at the pair table, and relaxing the pair table would convert a silent instrument failure into a published FALSE about a third party's networking.

verdict_rule: TRUE if a VPC-mode runtime without a NAT route fails image pull and succeeds with one; FALSE if egress is reachable either way
what_true_does_not_prove: that the runtime WORKS in a VPC — the image serves :80 and AgentCore's contract is POST /invocations and GET /ping on :8080, so no arm here produced a functioning runtime and none was needed: the comparison is differential

that a NAT gateway is the only way to supply the route — a VPC endpoint or an internet gateway on the private subnet would also carry the fetch, and this case measured one arrangement rather than enumerating them
anything about a CONTAINER image held in a private ECR repository, which needs an additional grant and, in a VPC with no route, an endpoint of its own

that the pull is the FIRST thing to fail without egress — it is the thing the seal names, and other steps may also fail; the arms are labelled by which step the service itself named, not by which step failed earliest
why_this_matters_operationally: The document's VPC guidance tells a reader that a private-subnet runtime needs a NAT route or an equivalent, which is advice with a cost attached: a NAT gateway bills hourly. Whether it is actually REQUIRED, and what the failure looks like when it is absent, is the difference between provisioning one on evidence and provisioning one on caution.
